title: CodeChallenge: Token count by subword length (part 2)

cues.en: This is the continuation of the code challenge that we started in the previous video.
cues.zh: 這支影片延續上一支影片開始的程式挑戰。

cues.zh: 所以，繼續之前，請先完成上一支影片，至少執行那些程式。

cues.en: This is the final serious exercise.
cues.zh: 這是最後一個比較認真的練習。

cues.en: There's going to be a very short exercise afterwards, but that's a little bit more fun and light hearted.
cues.zh: 之後還有一個很短的練習，不過比較輕鬆、有趣。

cues.en: Okay, so here in exercise five, the question we are investigating is whether more frequent words tend to have fewer tokens.
cues.zh: 練習五要探討的問題是，出現頻率較高的單字，是否往往需要較少 token。

cues.en: In other words, the words that appear more often in languages, at least in this text, and therefore the words that the tokenizer has seen more often during training.
cues.zh: 換句話說，語言中較常見的單字，至少在這段文字中較常見，因此 tokenizer 在訓練時見過較多次的單字，

cues.en: Do those words have fewer tokens?
cues.zh: 是不是有較少的 token？

cues.en: Now, before getting into this exercise, let me preemptively state that what we are doing here is more
cues.zh: 在進入練習之前，先說清楚，這裡的重點比較是

cues.en: about coding and working with Tokenizers than doing actual deep investigation into computational linguistics.
cues.zh: 寫程式與使用 tokenizer，而不是深入研究計算語言學。

cues.en: For one thing, we're only looking at one very specific text which is not representative of modern English.
cues.zh: 首先，只看一段非常特定的文字，並不能代表現代英文。

cues.en: And for another thing, the way that we are going to address this question actually includes a confound.
cues.zh: 其次，這裡回答問題的方式，其實包含一個混淆因素，

cues.en: So a problem with this experiment, the way we are doing it in this exercise.
cues.zh: 也就是這個練習中，實驗方法的一個問題。

cues.en: So I'd like you to see if you can identify that.
cues.zh: 希望你在解題時，能試著辨識這個

cues.en: Confound that problem while working through this exercise.
cues.zh: 混淆因素，也就是那個問題。

cues.en: And then I will discuss it later on.
cues.zh: 稍後我會討論。

cues.en: Anyway, the point is that the goal here is to focus on working with and visualizing tokenizers and tokenization.
cues.zh: 總之，這裡的目標，是專注使用 tokenizer，以及將斷詞結果視覺化。

cues.en: So the final result of this exercise is a plot that looks like this, where we have word frequency on the x axis and token length on the y axis.
cues.zh: 練習的最終結果，是像這樣的圖：x 軸為單字頻率，y 軸為 token 長度。

cues.en: Now, word frequency is simply the number of times that each of the unique words that we have split from the beginning of this code challenge appears in the text.
cues.zh: 單字頻率，就是這個程式挑戰開頭切分出的每個不重複單字，在文字中出現的次數。

cues.en: So the relationship between word frequency and token length is very clear visually here.
cues.zh: 圖中，單字頻率與 token 長度的關係非常清楚。

cues.en: The more often a token appears, the shorter its token length, so the fewer tokens it has.
cues.zh: 出現越頻繁，token 長度就越短，也就是需要的 token 越少。

cues.en: You can also print out some of the data in a list that looks like this.
cues.zh: 也可以把一些資料，印成像這樣的清單。

cues.en: So a comma appears over 2000 times and that's only one token.
cues.zh: 逗號出現超過 2,000 次，而且只有一個 token。

cues.en: Here we have the word that appearing 421 times.
cues.zh: that 這個字則出現 421 次，

cues.en: And so on.
cues.zh: 依此類推。

cues.en: Okay, so I hope you enjoy working through this exercise.
cues.zh: 希望你喜歡解這個練習。

cues.en: And now I will switch to code, show my solution, and also have a discussion about what this plot does and does not show and how you could improve this kind of investigation.
cues.zh: 接著，切換到程式展示解法，並討論這張圖能說明什麼、不能說明什麼，以及如何改善研究方式。

cues.en: Here I am transforming this set of unique words which we created in the previous exercise, into a list,
cues.zh: 這裡把上個練習建立的不重複單字集合，轉成串列，

cues.en: and that's just so we can index it.
cues.zh: 只是為了能使用索引。

cues.en: This is just for practical purposes.
cues.zh: 這純粹是實作考量。

cues.en: Okay.
cues.zh: 好。

cues.en: And then here is the vector initialized, where I'm going to count the number of times that each of these words appears in the text.
cues.zh: 接著，初始化這個向量，用來計算每個單字在文字中出現的次數，

cues.en: And the number of tokens that GPT four takes to encode each of these words.
cues.zh: 以及 GPT-4 編碼每個單字所需的 token 數。

cues.en: And then I just loop through.
cues.zh: 然後，直接走訪。

cues.en: So here, because this is a list.
cues.zh: 因為這裡是串列，

cues.en: Now I can use this count method.
cues.zh: 現在就能使用 count 方法。

cues.en: So this is just counting the number of times that each individual word in the set of unique words appears in the text.
cues.zh: 它只是計算不重複單字集合中，每個單字在文字裡出現的次數。

cues.en: And here is the length of the tokenization of that word.
cues.zh: 這裡則是該單字斷詞結果的長度。

cues.en: Pretty straightforward.
cues.zh: 相當直接。

cues.en: Takes a few seconds to calculate.
cues.zh: 計算需要幾秒鐘。

cues.en: And here is where I'm making the plot, and I'm setting the x axis to be logarithmically spaced.
cues.zh: 這裡繪圖，並把 x 軸設為對數尺度。

cues.en: You can also try this as a linear spacing, I think is just a little bit less clear.
cues.zh: 也可以試試線性尺度，但我覺得比較不清楚。

cues.en: You see, very often in computational sciences, when you are working with a very large range of numbers,
cues.zh: 計算科學中，當數值範圍非常大，

cues.en: that relationships are often easier to visualize and easier to understand when one or both dimensions is logarithmically scaled.
cues.zh: 常常將其中一個或兩個維度設為對數尺度，會更容易呈現及理解關係。

cues.en: Okay.
cues.zh: 好。

cues.en: So yeah.
cues.zh: 是的。

cues.en: And then here I'm just printing out some of the top examples here.
cues.zh: 這裡只是印出一些排名靠前的例子。

cues.en: So what do we see here.
cues.zh: 那麼，這裡看到什麼？

cues.en: And what is the problem with this investigation.
cues.zh: 這個研究又有什麼問題？

cues.en: The problem with this investigation is that we are mixing token length with token frequency, or I should say word length with word frequency.
cues.zh: 問題是，我們把 token 長度與 token 頻率混在一起，或者應該說，單字長度與單字頻率混在一起。

cues.en: So it is the case that the words that appear more often have shorter tokens or fewer tokens representing them.
cues.zh: 確實，較常出現的單字，token 較短，或者需要的 token 較少。

cues.en: But that's also because included in this list are punctuations like comma.
cues.zh: 但其中一部分，也因為清單包含逗號這類標點。

cues.en: So this word the and I and of and and these are valid words that we would want to include in this analysis punctuation.
cues.zh: the、I、of、and 等，都是分析時應該納入的有效單字。至於標點，

cues.en: It's debatable whether we want to skew this result according to, uh, you know, by including punctuation marks in here.
cues.zh: 是否該把它們納入，讓結果受其影響，就值得討論。

cues.en: Another potential confound here is that the shorter words necessarily require fewer tokens, because
cues.zh: 另一個可能的混淆因素，是較短的單字本來就需要較少 token，因為

cues.en: it's just fewer character pairs to identify during the byte pair encoding algorithm.
cues.zh: BPE 演算法中，需要辨識的字元配對比較少。

cues.en: So if you wanted to do this in a slightly more appropriate way, what you could do is separate this kind of a plot for different character word lengths.
cues.zh: 如果想用稍微更恰當的方式，可以依單字字元長度，分別畫這種圖。

cues.en: So that is to say, take all of the three letter words so and and the and was and generate this plot
cues.zh: 也就是取出所有三字母單字，例如 and、the、was，繪圖，

cues.en: and run an analysis only for three letter words.
cues.zh: 並且只分析三字母單字。

cues.en: And then you repeat this only for the four letter words, only for the five letter words.
cues.zh: 再對四字母、五字母單字，分別重複。

cues.en: And then you want to see if this kind of relationship still exists in words that are matched for character count.
cues.zh: 看看在字元數相同的單字之間，這種關係是否仍存在。

cues.en: That would be one approach to doing this analysis a little bit better.
cues.zh: 這是讓分析更完善的一種方法。

cues.en: Nonetheless, as I mentioned, the goal here is not to do a valid scientific experiment on computational linguistics.
cues.zh: 不過，如前所述，這裡的目標，不是做有效的計算語言學科學實驗。

cues.en: The goal is to gain more familiarity with Tokenizers and working with Tokenizers.
cues.zh: 而是更熟悉 tokenizer，以及如何使用它。

cues.en: Well, this was a really long code challenge and I think it was quite challenging.
cues.zh: 這個程式挑戰真的很長，我也覺得相當有挑戰性。

cues.en: So I wanted to include one more exercise in here, just to have a little bit of fun and also improving your coding and text processing skills, but mostly fun.
cues.zh: 所以，想再加入一個練習，輕鬆玩一下，也改善程式與文字處理能力，但主要還是好玩。

cues.en: Okay.
cues.zh: 好。

cues.en: It's very simple.
cues.zh: 很簡單。

cues.en: Pick three tokens from the GPT tokenizer completely at random, then join them together.
cues.zh: 從 GPT tokenizer 完全隨機挑出三個 token，再把它們接起來。

cues.en: So join the three tokens together without any whitespace in between and just see what you come up with.
cues.zh: 串接三個 token，中間不加空白，看看會得到什麼。

cues.en: So here is one example.
cues.zh: 這裡是一個例子。

cues.en: So these are three random tokens common bomb and the Greek character phi.
cues.zh: 這三個隨機 token，是 common、bomb，以及希臘字母 phi。

cues.en: And so then I combine these together.
cues.zh: 接著，把它們組合起來。

cues.en: In this case there are no spaces here, and the fake word that I generated is common bumf.
cues.zh: 這個例子沒有空白，產生了 common bumf 這個假字（拼字辨識待核）。

cues.en: I thought that was pretty nice.
cues.zh: 我覺得滿不錯的。

cues.en: Here's another word.
cues.zh: 還有另一個字。

cues.en: This one was even funnier.
cues.zh: 這個更好笑。

cues.en: Space.
cues.zh: 空白，

cues.en: Live lives and space flakes.
cues.zh: 接著 live、lives，以及空白加 flakes（片段拼字辨識待核）。

cues.en: Then I combine these into one word removing the space.
cues.zh: 再把它們組成一個字，移除空白。

cues.en: And this, I thought, was a really interesting word.
cues.zh: 我覺得這個字非常有意思，

cues.en: Live stanger's flakes.
cues.zh: 也就是 live stanger’s flakes（拼字辨識待核）。

cues.en: That's how I interpreted this.
cues.zh: 我是這樣解讀的。

cues.en: And then, you know, I thought this was pretty funny.
cues.zh: 接著，覺得這實在很好笑，

cues.en: So I asked ChatGPT what this word might mean.
cues.zh: 就問 ChatGPT，這個字可能是什麼意思。

cues.en: And yeah, there's a lot of text here, but the upshot is that it could mean a quirky, unpredictable
cues.zh: 這裡文字很多，但重點是，它可能表示一種古怪、不可預測的

cues.en: experience or thing which definitely describes the experience of working with modern language models.
cues.zh: 經驗或事物；這確實很符合使用現代語言模型的經驗。

cues.en: Anyway, so I hope you have some fun with this exercise.
cues.zh: 希望你也享受這個練習。

cues.zh: 如果產生有趣、新奇的字，歡迎貼到問答區。

cues.en: So here I'm setting a parameter for the number of tokens.
cues.zh: 這裡設定 token 數量的參數。

cues.en: So if you like, If you want to create longer words, you can just increase this number.
cues.zh: 如果想產生更長的字，可以增加這個數字。

cues.zh: 好。

cues.en: And then I choose three tokens at random from the vocabulary or three token indices.
cues.zh: 接著，從詞彙表隨機選三個 token，也就是三個 token 索引。

cues.en: And here I print out what each of those tokens are.
cues.zh: 這裡印出每個 token 的內容。

cues.en: Friendly reminder again that when you're using decoders you cannot use individual numbers.
cues.zh: 再次提醒，使用解碼器時，不能輸入單獨的數字。

cues.zh: 這裡必須輸入串列，

cues.zh: 否則會出錯。

cues.en: Okay, so if you're working with single tokens that you want to decode, you just need to put this that number into square brackets okay.
cues.zh: 所以，要解碼單個 token，只需要把那個數字放進方括號。

cues.en: And then this is already a list here.
cues.zh: 而這裡本來就已經是串列，

cues.en: So we don't need to embed it inside another list.
cues.zh: 所以不必再包進另一個串列。

cues.zh: 結果得到這個字。我甚至不想嘗試念它，以免出糗，但看起來確實很有趣。

cues.en: Well, that was quite an intense code challenge, but I hope you enjoyed it and feel that you are now more comfortable working with text and tokenizers.
cues.zh: 這個程式挑戰相當密集，不過希望你喜歡，也覺得現在更能自在處理文字與 tokenizer。

cues.en: A key take home point is that words in tokens are not the same thing.
cues.zh: 一個重要重點是，單字與 token 並不相同。

cues.en: There are cases where individual tokens correspond to individual words, but that's not the right way to think about text tokenization.
cues.zh: 有時，個別 token 確實對應個別單字，但不該以此作為理解文字斷詞的方式。

cues.en: This is a point that I'm going to stress many times early on in this course, because we humans think about language in terms of words.
cues.zh: 課程前段會多次強調這一點，因為人類是以單字來思考語言。

cues.en: But language models do not actually process words.
cues.zh: 但語言模型實際上不處理單字，

cues.en: They don't think about words.
cues.zh: 不以單字思考，

cues.en: They're not trained on words.
cues.zh: 不是以單字作為訓練單位，

cues.en: They don't generate words.
cues.zh: 也不是直接產生單字。

cues.en: They only work with tokens and the embeddings that are created from those tokens.
cues.zh: 它只處理 token，以及由 token 建立的嵌入。

cues.en: And so a lot of behaviors of llms that initially seem confusing actually make a lot of sense when you
cues.zh: 因此，許多一開始令人困惑的 LLM 行為，在你理解

cues.en: realize the distinction between words and tokens, including a fun little demo that I will highlight in the next video.
cues.zh: 單字與 token 的差別後，就會變得合理，包括下一支影片要特別展示的一個有趣小示範。
